findings.description: Three skip rules added to the Bash path-word scan in check_value run before os.path.normpath and before the SENSITIVE / allowed-roots test in outside(). (1) The 1.2.4 rule `if w.startswith("/."): continue` is meant for repo-relative /.claude/ references, but it also drops any word of the form /./<dir>/... or /../<dir>/..., which the shell resolves to /<dir>/... (normpath would turn /./root/x into /root/x, which SENSITIVE matches). (2) after_closing_quote returns True whenever body[pos-2] is not whitespace or a separator; when body[pos-2] is itself a quote character the token before the path is an empty quoted string, so the word is a complete absolute path, not a tail. (3) The 1.2.1 one-component rule treats /<name> as a slash command unless <name> is in SENSITIVE_SINGLE, but ABS_WORD stops at glob characters (* ? [), so a sensitive component whose last characters are globbed is read as a non-sensitive one-component word and skipped. Grader 1.2.0 flagged all three shapes as outside_path; 1.2.7 reports them clean. The scan is the grader's integrity signal that the agent under test did not read outside its sandbox.
findings.failure_mode: A run whose Bash tool_use reached a sensitive root through a dot-segment, an empty-quote prefix, or a globbed component is graded with contaminated = null and its row counts as a scored trial, so the batch's recall and hidden-test figures can include a leaked run.
findings.suggested_fix: Normalize first: compute n = os.path.normpath(w) and apply the dot-dir skip only when n still begins with '/.' (a true root dot-dir). In after_closing_quote, return False when body[pos-2] is a quote character (an empty string before the path). For the one-component rule, treat the word as a candidate when the character right after the match is a glob metacharacter (* ? [), or extend ABS_WORD's character class to include glob characters and strip them before the sensitive test. Add bats cases for each shape asserting outside_path.

findings.description: For Bash tool inputs the hidden check moved from a case-insensitive substring to HIDDEN_TOKEN / HIDDEN_GLOB, which require HIDDEN in capitals, an adjacent path or identifier character, a camelCase continuation, or a glob character. The comment accepts `pytest -k hidden` as the bare-argument gap, but the rule equally exempts a bare directory argument: `cd hidden`, `ls hidden`, `cat hidden`, or `find . -name hidden` carry the word with only whitespace or a separator around it and are not hits, while the same directory reached as tests/hidden is. Read/Grep/Glob inputs still use the substring, so only Bash is relaxed.
findings.failure_mode: An agent that changes into or lists a directory literally named hidden through Bash is not flagged, while the Read tool on the same path would be; the contamination result depends on which tool the agent chose.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the bare-word exemption narrow: exempt `hidden` only when it is the argument of -k/-m (pytest selectors) and otherwise flag a bare `hidden` that is the direct argument of cd, ls, cat, find -name/-path, or a shell redirect. Alternatively read the hidden tests directory name from task.yaml and flag any Bash word equal to it or ending in it.

findings.description: strip_heredocs removes heredoc bodies before the absolute-path scan, including bodies fed to python3, python, bash, sh, node, perl or ruby (count_interpreter_heredocs only counts them). Code in such a body opens whatever path it names. The comment justifies the gap by the container executor, where the sensitive roots are empty, and notes host grading needs LOA_EVAL_ALLOW_HOST_GRADING=1. In host mode the same gap is a real missed leak: an interpreter heredoc can read the suite root or the hidden tests on the host and the path scan never sees it; the hidden/suite_path/repo_name substring scans do read the body but are string-literal checks.
findings.failure_mode: Under host grading a run that read hidden material from an interpreter heredoc body is graded clean; heredoc_interpreters is telemetry and does not affect contaminated.
findings.suggested_fix: When A.executor == "host", scan heredoc bodies whose operator command is an interpreter with ABS_WORD (accept the prose false-positive risk there, since host mode is already an opt-in), or at minimum treat heredoc_interpreters > 0 together with a sensitive path word anywhere in the body as a contamination hit in host mode. Document the residual gap in the --help text next to LOA_EVAL_ALLOW_HOST_GRADING.

findings.description: DEC-0545 changes degraded from 'any models_used key differs from model_requested' to 'the requested model is absent from a non-empty models_used'. A phase whose models_used contains the requested model with a token count of 1 and another model with the rest is now not degraded, and the row carries no per-model token share. The run-ablation.sh header applies the same rule to the drift guard, with extra models recorded as telemetry only. The row therefore cannot distinguish a WebFetch summariser from a provider-side substitution that still touched the requested model once.
findings.failure_mode: A substituted phase whose transcript shows the requested model for even one turn is rowed degraded = false and the batch report treats it as a clean trial of the arm.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the degraded test share-aware: compute the requested model's fraction of models_used output tokens per phase and degrade when it is below a threshold (e.g. 0.5), or when any non-requested model's tokens exceed the requested model's. Emit the per-model token map in the row so the report can audit extra models.
